title: Red fox near Pinehurst Dr
body: A red fox (Vulpes vulpes) photographed in Pinehurst Dr, Wilmington, DE, US. Field notes from the observation: Pretty bad mange. Red foxes are the largest of the true foxes and live on every continent except Antarctica.

title: Red fox near Кирилловский р-н
body: A red fox (Vulpes vulpes) photographed in Кирилловский р-н, Вологодская обл., Россия. Field notes from the observation: Снято фотоловушкой у гнезда лугового чекана. A red fox can hear a mouse move under a meter of snow and pounces in a high arc to catch it.

title: Red fox near Wellington Township
body: A red fox (Vulpes vulpes) photographed in Wellington Township, OH 44090, USA. The observation record carries no extra notes — the photo speaks for itself. Fox kits are born blind in spring dens and emerge at about one month old.

title: Gray wolf near Konya
body: A gray wolf (Canis lupus) photographed in Konya, TR. Field notes from the observation: Location: Ankara, Türkiye Elevation (m): Notes: Observed with care. During the observation period, no harm or disturbance was inflicted upon the observed organis…. Gray wolves live in family packs led by a breeding pair, and their howls can carry for miles.

title: Gray wolf near Leh (Ladakh)
body: A gray wolf (Canis lupus) photographed in Leh (Ladakh), IN-JK, IN. Field notes from the observation: ATTAQUE EN MEUTE AVEC DES JEUNES SUR UN CHIEN DE NOMADE. Wolves were reintroduced to Yellowstone in 1995, and elk herds changed their behavior within years.

title: Gray wolf near Cook County
body: A gray wolf (Canis lupus) photographed in Cook County, US-MN, US. Field notes from the observation: On a trail through a boreal forest. A wolf's paws are larger than a domestic dog's, an adaptation for traveling snow.

title: Dog near La Ceja
body: A dog (Canis familiaris) photographed in La Ceja, Antioquia, CO. Field notes from the observation: JN. Domestic dogs descended from wolves and were the first animals humans tamed.

title: Dog near Viñedos el Álamo
body: A dog (Canis familiaris) photographed in Viñedos el Álamo, Saltillo, Coah., México. The observation record carries no extra notes — the photo speaks for itself. Dogs read human gestures like pointing better than any other species, including chimpanzees.

title: Dog near Хохольский р-н
body: A dog (Canis familiaris) photographed in Хохольский р-н, Воронежская обл., Россия. The observation record carries no extra notes — the photo speaks for itself. Puppies open their eyes at about two weeks, and early socialization shapes a calm adult.

title: Brown bear near Anchorage County
body: A brown bear (Ursus arctos) photographed in Anchorage County, US-AK, US. Field notes from the observation: The brown bear mama And her three growing cubs cross The creek on patrol. Brown bears are omnivores that fatten on salmon, berries, and roots before winter dens.

title: Brown bear near Hoonah-Angoon Census Area
body: A brown bear (Ursus arctos) photographed in Hoonah-Angoon Census Area, Alaska, USA. Recorded field tags: Inner passage, Pavlof Harbor, Stilla havet, usa, Alaska. A bear's heart rate drops sharply during winter sleep, and cubs are born while the mother dozes.

title: Brown bear near Teton County
body: A brown bear (Ursus arctos) photographed in Teton County, US-WY, US. The observation record carries no extra notes — the photo speaks for itself. Despite their size, brown bears can sprint at speeds over 30 miles per hour.

title: White-tailed deer near Crazy Grouse Lane
body: A white-tailed deer (Odocoileus virginianus) photographed in Crazy Grouse Lane, South Londonderry, VT, US. The observation record carries no extra notes — the photo speaks for itself. Male white-tailed deer grow and shed antlers each year, clashing during the autumn rut.

title: White-tailed deer near E Cornwall Rd
body: A white-tailed deer (Odocoileus virginianus) photographed in E Cornwall Rd, Cary, NC, US. The observation record carries no extra notes — the photo speaks for itself. A startled deer bounds away in explosive zigzags, and its white tail flags the danger to others.

title: White-tailed deer near Bristol
body: A white-tailed deer (Odocoileus virginianus) photographed in Bristol, PA 19007, USA. The observation record carries no extra notes — the photo speaks for itself. Deer ears swivel independently toward every rustle in the underbrush.

title: Snow leopards of the high Himalaya
body: The snow leopard stalks cliff faces above 3,000 meters, ghost-gray against the rock. Few big cats are so hard to photograph in the wild.
